premise: Tamriel, 3E 430 — two years before the Emperor's line falters and everything cracks open. The Third Empire under Uriel Septim VII still holds the provinces together, but the seams show: the Elder Council schemes for succession no one will say aloud, the Thalmor's Aldmeri Dominion watches from across the Abecean with patient hunger, Daedric cults work in the dark beneath temple floors, and old grudges between Nord, Dunmer, Redguard, and Imperial simmer under a thin Imperial peace. A D&D-style class-and-level game, reskinned so it plays like Elder Scrolls: guild-based magic (Mages Guild schools of Destruction/Restoration/Illusion/etc.), Aedra/Daedra cosmology underpinning divine and infernal magic, and racial/cultural identity that actually matters mechanically and socially.
tone: Balanced mix — political intrigue and guild/court scheming share the stage with frontier adventure (ruins, bandits, Daedric shrines, monster hunts) and dark mythic undercurrents (the Daedric Princes are real, watching, and transactional; Dwemer ruins hold Aylied-and-older wrongness). Scene-to-scene, follow the players.
magic: High and structured — magic is common, guild-taught, and schooled (Alteration, Conjuration, Destruction, Illusion, Mysticism, Restoration), but never casual: every spell traces back to Aedra-granted order or Daedra-granted power, and both sides collect on what they lend.
setting: Established high-fantasy IP adaptation — all of Tamriel, opening in Cyrodiil, playable across every province.
genre_bend: Elder Scrolls' actual bend, kept intact rather than filed down to generic fantasy: Aedra/Daedra cosmology where 'divine' and 'demonic' magic are the same currency spent by different lenders; guild politics (Mages Guild, Fighters Guild, Thieves Guild, Dark Brotherhood) as the real seat of power alongside noble houses; race as lived culture (Nord/Breton/Redguard/Imperial/Dunmer/Altmer/Bosmer/Khajiit/Argonian/Orsimer, each with real customs, biases, and homeland politics) rather than a stat bonus; Dwemer ruins as cold, alien, un-magical technology nobody living understands.
voice_exemplar: In-world Elder Scrolls loremaster — the dry, faux-historical, slightly self-important register of TES's own in-game books and loading-screen apocrypha; a chronicler who footnotes rumor as fact and fact as rumor.
art_style: In the style of a gilded Third Era Imperial Library manuscript illumination — hand-tooled leather and beaten-gold linework — but rendered with the grim painterly weight of a Rembrandt oil, so every illustration reads like a priceless, slightly too-honest history painting smuggled out of the Imperial Palace archives.
chronicler_persona: A Cyrodiilic cloister-scribe of the Imperial Geographical Society, pompous and footnote-happy, convinced every scene he renders is Historically Significant — he editorializes in his captions, contradicts himself between volumes, and never met a rumor he wouldn't illustrate as fact.

axes.bend: All nine-plus provinces of Tamriel sketched, Cyrodiil detailed first (Imperial City, the Gold Road, the Heartlands, the Imperial Reserve), with real travel friction between provinces.

Elder Council succession maneuvering, the four adventuring guilds (Mages/Fighters/Thieves/Dark Brotherhood), Daedric cult cells, Thalmor Aldmeri Dominion agents operating quietly, provincial houses (Dunmer Great Houses, Nord jarldoms, Redguard Crowns/Forebears schism).
Tiber Septim's founding of the Empire, the Camoran Usurper's rebellion, the Warp in the West, and the slow-building cracks of 3E 430 that foreshadow (without yet triggering) the Emperor's fall.
Aedra/Daedra dual cosmology; the six-plus schools of magic as guild-taught curricula; Daedric Princes as real, present, transactional patrons with named domains and prices.
Each playable race as a living culture with homeland politics, customs, and inter-racial friction (not a stat block) — Nord/Breton/Redguard/Imperial/Dunmer/Altmer/Bosmer/Khajiit/Argonian/Orsimer.
Daedra (scamps to dremora), undead (draugr, ghosts, liches), and provincial wildlife — enough named threats to populate frontier play without exhausting the axis.
Dwemer ruins and animunculi — cold, alien, un-magical artifice that nobody living fully understands; a wonder and a hazard, not a tech tree.
